questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore a new culture in Asia, as I had not been there for a long time. Taiwan seemed like an ideal choice, as the University of Copenhagen and National Taiwan University have an exchange agreement, and I also have family connections there

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can only recommend it!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy overall. People in Taiwan were generally very helpful, which made the experience much easier.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I lived in a dorm with local Taiwanese students who helped me a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: none

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Didn't live on or close to NTU main campus and I found housing through my host institution.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transport is clean, runs on time, and is overall very efficient, so I would not stress too much about not living on or close to the main campus. Many students do not live on campus, and I never felt excluded from any opportunities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: none

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: none

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It went smoothly. I felt that the connections I made during the introduction week helped me navigate the registration process and consult others about potential oversights.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Older students, other exchange students, NTU personel etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get all of my top priorities, but I was able to enroll in all the classes I needed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start looking for and selecting courses well in advance. Since you cannot select too many courses and may not get all the courses you want or expect, it is a good idea to have a Plan B or even a Plan C.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: it was generally very different from what I was used to but overall good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: MA courses required more preparation, particularly in terms of readings and reflective assignments. As a result, I had to invest more time in MA courses than in BA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classroom teaching was largely similar to that at UCPH. However, mandatory attendance and the number of reflective assignments differed significantly. In contrast to most courses at UCPH, where the final grade is typically determined by the final exam, grades in these courses were accumulated throughout the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of clubs that you could join. I joined the NTU gym which was cheap and created a good oppertunity to talk and mingle with others.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go hiking and see some of the beautiful nature! Definetly try karaoke.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking and see some of the beautiful nature! Definetly try karaoke.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The locals were very kind and helpful, which made the experience quite easy overall.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to reach out in a calm and collected manner, perhaps by asking a classmate sitting next to you. There may be a language barrier, but most students are willing to give English a try. Often, they also take the initiative to approach you, so do not be afraid to interact.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How nice and helpful they were. Really made you feel welcome.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared to attend most classes, as attendance may affect your final grade.
Keep an open mind and take the initiative to explore—Taiwan, its people, and fellow students have so much to offer, so do not hesitate to seek it out.
And enjoy the food.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many different people greatly broadened my horizons.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sleep, social and study balance.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Nope

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
